title: Continuous telemetry enables linkage of sessions and contexts to the same wearer
description: The wearable receives a rich, continuous stream of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps from the wearer. Even if explicit identifiers are absent, the combination of persistent sensor patterns, location traces, and time information can allow records from different moments or contexts to be linked to the same individual.
assumptions: The device or associated system stores or processes telemetry in a way that preserves temporal continuity or stable device/user association.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include a specific Linkability node.

title: Sensor telemetry can identify the wearer
description: GPS traces, timestamps, activity patterns, and physiological telemetry may directly or indirectly identify the wearer. Home/work locations and habitual movement patterns are especially identifying, making the incoming flow privacy-sensitive even before any explicit account registration.
assumptions: Telemetry is retained, observable, or combined with other data available to the device or backend.
uncertainty_note: Specific Identifiability node citation is approximate; retrieved context only confirmed this threat type is applicable for ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: The flow discloses sensitive personal information beyond raw measurements
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps can reveal sensitive facts such as health condition, exercise habits, daily routines, places visited, religious attendance, workplace, home address, and social relationships. The privacy risk arises from what can be inferred from the transmitted telemetry.
assumptions: The device or downstream components can access, store, or analyze the telemetry over time.
uncertainty_note: Specific Disclosure node id is best-effort; the retrieved context did not provide a more granular D node.

title: Continuous collection exceeds data minimization for initial device operation
description: Capturing GPS position, timestamps, heart rate, and step counts continuously may collect more personal data, at higher frequency, and for longer duration than is strictly necessary for some wearable functions. This creates a detectability risk because the system can observe the wearer's presence, movements, and bodily state continuously.
assumptions: Not all listed telemetry is strictly necessary at all times for the intended feature set, and collection begins by default while wearing the device.
uncertainty_note: Detectability vs. disclosure can overlap here; node id is approximate because no specific Dd node was retrieved.

title: Wearer may be unaware they are sharing continuous personal telemetry
description: The wearer may not fully understand that simply wearing the device results in ongoing sharing of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps with the device process, potentially continuously and in the background. They may also be unaware of the granularity and sensitivity of what is captured.
assumptions: Notice, onboarding, or just-in-time indicators are insufficiently clear about continuous sensing and the categories of data collected.

title: Continuous telemetry capture may occur without valid or sufficiently specific consent
description: Because the flow involves continuous collection of sensitive and location-related telemetry, the system may process data without freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent, or without another appropriate legal basis. Bundled acceptance or default-on sensing would increase this risk.
assumptions: The product relies on consent or another legal basis that may not adequately cover continuous GPS and health-related telemetry collection.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance node id is approximate; retrieved context did not include the detailed Nc tree.

title: Excessive disclosure of precise activity and location data to the companion app
description: The wearable sync includes exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps. Sending precise GPS traces together with persistent device id and timestamps to the companion app may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for core synchronization, especially if full-resolution traces or stable identifiers are not required for all app features.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app does not strictly need full-fidelity GPS traces and a persistent device identifier for every sync operation, and that data minimization alternatives exist (e.g., coarse location, rotating identifiers, reduced timestamp precision).
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgment based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimization structure; retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->Process flows but does not provide the exact sub-node text.

title: Linkability of sync batches across sessions via device id and timestamps
description: A persistent device id combined with repeated sensor uploads and timestamps can allow the companion app to link multiple exercise sessions and GPS traces to the same individual or device over time, enabling longitudinal profiling beyond what may be necessary for basic sync.
assumptions: Assumes the device id is stable across syncs and visible to the app, and that the app can correlate batches over time.
